findings.conclusion: insert_file_data_impl changes only its existing snapshot_leaf_batches branch. SnapshotWriteTxn::write_file_data selects this true branch. Other existing incremental/deferred/config entrypoints and public_surface::insert_on -> replace_on retain false selection. Only cardinality >=8 enters the new dependency helper; smaller sets keep the original single-row loop.

Independently compared the complete shared resolution preparation region: original clone, normalize, validate, serialize, payload-byte rejection, DELETE and manifest INSERT/digest are exact bytes in their original order. Public surface normalization, identity check and insertion are likewise exact bytes. Invalid manifest rejection still precedes the dependency DELETE, not necessarily every earlier file/public-surface write, which was also true before.

The existing normalized manifest BTreeSet is iterated directly, preserving all kind/key pairs and original ordering. The new binder emits the same file_path, DependencyKind::as_str and key into plain INSERT without an added conflict policy. It never collects the full file's references or spans files. No schema/index/read-path, dependency omission, normalization or deduplication rule changes.

The original bounded_rows accepts an iterator so BTreeSet and slices both borrow entries. Its size/flush/oversize-single-row loop is unchanged. Actual repeated file/kind/key SQL payload bytes pass through the original payload_bytes implementation. At most64 references/64KiB ordinary bound-value payload are held; a legal larger single row remains accepted alone. The unchanged multi_insert tiers64/8/1 bind3columns, at most192parameters, with no new SQL arities beyond those tiers.

All six existing snapshot leaf helpers keep their call bodies. Slice/Vec reference iterators have exact size hints matching the former len and emptiness checks; iterator generalization changes neither their element order nor flush conditions. Existing payload and failure-window tests remain in the file unchanged.

Batch errors propagate with ? through the unchanged file loop and existing rebuild transaction. The unchanged execute_temp_db_staging_build drops the failed transaction and performs existing staging cleanup before any swap. Existing index generation/floor, CAS, swap, pragmas and transaction ownership files are not modified. A failed multi-row statement may have a different uncommitted prefix from separate statements; this is not accepted partial state or permission to catch the error and commit.

The new end-to-end failure control exercises the real temp/WAL rebuild and unchanged live rows/generation, not physical rollback under DirectWriter journal_mode=OFF. The latter's existing failure propagation remains unchanged and no stronger guarantee is claimed.

Two unit controls compare original per-row SQL to the new helper using actual rowid/all-column equality and SQLite StatementStatus::Run at0/1/7/8/9/63/64/65/73/129/4096 rows, all7 kinds and duplicate BTreeSet insertion; byte-limited windows and legal oversize single SQL values are also exercised. Two integration controls compare real original/full-snapshot rebuild manifests/surfaces/rows and generation, subsequent ordinary incremental replacement, and injected key70 failure plus version999 rejection with unchanged live state and matching errors. These controls are prepared, not executed.

The final-live-state equality in a rollback test does not by itself prove validation preceded DELETE. This order is established in this review by exact source-region comparison. The author receipt distinguishes these scopes.

These six paths are disjoint from the separately reviewed two oracle paths. Both candidates preserve the same dependency table contents and original oracle admission/serialization/comparison gates. There is no skipped parity check or measured performance result.

allowed_next_step: Root may combine these exact six blobs with the independently reviewed oracle blobs and construct a new source-admission chain for the existing original CI. Frozen PR176 G is not mutated or re-certified here.
